messages:
maria-cs: Hey team — customer (acme-retail) reports embeddings API throwing dimension errors and big latency for batch uploads. Started after they switched to eu-west endpoint. They say some requests succeed and others fail with "DimensionMismatchError". Posting logs and repro below.

maria-cs: Logs: 
```
2026-03-14T14:22:03Z ERROR id=xyz DimensionMismatchError: expected_dim=1536 got=1024 payload_id=abc123 route=embeddings/eu-west
2026-03-14T14:22:03Z WARN id=xyz BatchSize=256 latency_ms=1800 origin=customer
2026-03-14T14:22:05Z ERROR id=xyz 429 TooManyRequests fallback=us-east
```

maria-cs: Repro steps provided by customer:
1) curl to https://api.eu-west.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"embed-compact-1536","input":["doc1","doc2", ... up to 256]}'.
2) intermittent failures, sometimes returns error above. Throughput dropped.

maria-cs: They also pasted this client error: 
```
Error: Received vector length 1024 but model expects 1536
    at embeddings.generate (/node_modules/redwood-sdk/index.js:45:12)
```

samir-eng: Thanks Maria. Two immediate hypotheses: 1) wrong model->region mismatch (client hitting eu-west but model variant in us-east) causing on-the-fly fallback to a different model with different dim; 2) batching/concurrent merging is incorrectly trimming/padding vectors for certain node types.

eli-infra: Also possible routing spillover — we had a capacity blip in eu-west earlier today and some requests were routed to us-east fallback pool. If client pinned model name without exact variant, fallback could return a different embedding dim.

anna-ps: Customer said they use our hosted key and didn't set dedicated routing. They did say they tried to increase batch size to 256 to speed up ingestion. That could exacerbate cold start batching behavior.

samir-eng: Can we get the exact model identifier the customer used? If they used shorthand like "embed-compact-1536" vs full canonical id "redwood/embed-compact-1536@v2" a fallback could map to an older variant.

maria-cs: They sent request body: {"model":"embed-compact-1536","input": [..256 strings..], "batch_size": 128} and the SDK shows it translates to endpoint /v1/embeddings (region eu-west).

ricardo-sre: Pulling routing logs now. I see on 2026-03-14T14:21:58Z a burst and autoscaler in eu-west couldn't spin up nodes fast enough. Some percentage (~12%) was routed to fallback pool in us-east which hosts embed-legacy-1024. That explains the 1024 dims.

ops-bot: Incident alert: eu-west GPU pool autoscale_failure 14:20-14:28. Affected: embeddings route (hosted). TicketID: INC-2026-314.

samir-eng: Two parallel fixes: 1) Customer side: pin the exact model variant with full id and reduce batch_size to 32 to avoid mixing partial batches during cold starts. 2) Platform side: add a stronger validation early — if model claims 1536 and returned vectors are 1024, return a deterministic 400 with a clear message instead of attempting silent fallback.

eli-infra: For immediate mitigation, we can change routing policy for hosted keys to avoid cross-region fallback for embeddings (respect region header); that will cause 429s instead of dimension errors but is safer. Can we do an emergency config toggle?

ricardo-sre: Yes, we have a config flag route.allow_cross_region_fallback=false we can flip for the eu-west tenant set. But note this will increase client-visible throttling until capacity recovers.

anna-ps: I'll coordinate with the CS customer-facing message: explain why dimension mismatch happened, recommend pinning full model id + lower batch, and offer temporary dedicated capacity if they need large ingest and low latency.

maria-cs: Customer asked for repro checks we can run. Suggested steps I posted: 1) call single-item request to eu-west to confirm dim 1536. 2) run a 50-item batch with batch_size=32. 3) inspect response headers X-Redwood-Region and X-Redwood-Model-Variant.

samir-eng: Good. Also ask them to attach the base64 of one returned vector that errored so we can verify length and rule out client-side truncation. JS SDK bug once trimmed buffer in older Node versions could return wrong length.

eli-infra: Action items for infra: (a) flip route.allow_cross_region_fallback=false for eu-west tenant group (will push in 5m after approvals), (b) add a short-term rule that rejects cross-region fallbacks for embedding routes with 400 + helpful body, (c) autoscaler: add faster warm pool spin-up for embedding-critical pools.

ricardo-sre: I'll file a postmortem entry into INC-2026-314 and tag the embedding capacity chart. We might need a hot-cache of warm workers to reduce cold start latency from ~600ms to <100ms.

maria-cs: Customer wants ETA. Can we promise immediate toggle + config change and a follow-up on autoscaler improvements?

anna-ps: Yes — we can toggle now and I'll message the customer with steps to retest. Samir, can you draft the message wording?

samir-eng: Draft: "We identified cross-region fallback during a eu-west capacity blip which caused some requests to be served by an older embed variant (1024-dim). We've toggled routing to prevent cross-region fallback for embeddings and recommend pinning the canonical model id (e.g., redwood/embed-compact-1536@v2) and reducing batch_size to 32 while we restore warm capacity in eu-west. If you'd like, we can provision temporary dedicated capacity for your ingest window."

maria-cs: Putting that message to the customer now. I'll also ask them to run the three repro steps and paste headers & any returned vectors that look wrong.

ops-bot: Action taken: route.allow_cross_region_fallback set to false for tenant_group=hosted-eu-west by ricardo-sre at 2026-03-14T14:30:02Z.

samir-eng: Follow-ups: ticket to eng-runtime to add a schema validation step: after vector generation check len == model.expected_dim and if mismatch then fail fast. Also add metrics for percent of cross-region-served embeddings.

maria-cs: Customer confirmed reduced errors after we toggled the routing but saw increased 429s during peak. They accepted temporary dedicated trial. Closing loop once dedicated is provisioned or autoscaler improved.

ricardo-sre: Marking this thread for postmortem. INC-2026-314 link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-314

maria-cs: Thanks everyone. If customer provides a sample bad vector I'll attach to the incident for debugging. :thumbsup:
